To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cooling flow flattens the iron abundance distribution and that the variety of the observed iron abundance distribution can be accounted for by the combination of the cooling flow and the turbulence produced by galactocentric motions.

(i) the iron abundance distribution in a cluster of galaxies is determined by the cooling flow velocity and by the velocity dispersion of galaxies in the cluster, and (ii) the iron abundance in the cluster center is higher for the clusters with higher velocity dispersion of galaxies.

(i) the iron abundance distribution is flattened by cooling flow if the velocity of the flow is sufficiently large and (ii) the observed variety of iron abundance distribution can be explained by the effect of cooling flow.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following two topics.
the study of the iron distribution in clusters of galaxies.
the study of the iron distribution in clusters of galaxies and the influence of the cooling flow and the turbulence produced by galatic motion on it.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the iron abundance distribution is flattened if the cluster is dynamically active.
the observed iron abundance distribution is a consequence of the combination of galactic motion, the cooling flow and the initial distribution of iron in the intracluster medium.

, if the cooling flow is not present or if its velocity is sufficiently small, the iron abundance distribution is not affected by the cooling flow and reflects the initial distribution of iron, which was probably produced by supernovae in the early stage of the cluster formation, while if the cooling flow exists with a velocity of the order of 1000km/s or more, the iron abundance is flattened by the cooling flow.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the iron abundance distribution is determined mainly by the cooling flow velocity and the turbulence produced by galatic motion.
a large cooling flow and/or a small velocity of galactic motions are necessary to explain the iron abundance distribution in clusters of galaxies.
the observed iron abundance distribution is determined by a competition between the effect of cooling flow and the effect of galactic motion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the iron abundance distribution is sensitive to the cooling flow, and that the iron abundance is not necessarily an accurate measure of the metal abundance.
the iron abundance distribution is not a simple function of the cluster mass, but it is also sensitive to the cluster dynamical state.

the iron abundance distribution is strongly affected by cooling flows and galactic motion, and therefore, the iron abundance distribution alone is not enough to determine the origin of the observed iron.
